title: Q3 Enterprise Sales Strategy Review
summary: Sales leadership met to review pipeline health, discuss pricing adjustments for the enterprise tier, and align on key account strategies. The team identified 3 at-risk accounts and agreed to implement a new discount approval workflow.

topics.name: Pipeline Health
topics.insight: Q3 pipeline is at 78% of target. Mid-market segment overperforming (+15%) while enterprise segment is lagging (-22%). Need focused outreach on enterprise leads.

topics.name: Enterprise Pricing Model
topics.insight: Current per-seat pricing creates friction for large deployments (500+ seats). Volume tiers with annual commitment discounts reduce sales cycle length by 30%.

topics.name: Competitive Positioning
topics.insight: Two new competitors entered the market with freemium models. Our differentiator remains compliance certifications (SOC2, HIPAA) which competitors lack.

topics.name: Customer Churn Analysis
topics.insight: Churn rate spiked to 8.2% in Q2. Root cause: poor onboarding experience for teams >50 users. Need dedicated onboarding specialists for enterprise accounts.

decisions.decision: Introduce 3-tier enterprise pricing: Starter (50-200 seats), Growth (200-1000 seats), Scale (1000+ seats).
decisions.reason: Simplifies quoting, allows reps to close deals without custom pricing approval for standard tiers. Reduces approval cycle from 5 days to same-day.

decisions.decision: Require VP approval for discounts exceeding 20% off list price.
decisions.reason: Prevents margin erosion. Historical data shows deals with >20% discount have 40% lower renewal rates.

decisions.decision: Launch dedicated onboarding program for accounts with 100+ seats.
decisions.reason: Directly addresses Q2 churn spike. Estimated 3-month payback period based on reduced churn projections.

actionItems.task: Publish updated enterprise pricing tiers to sales playbook and CRM
Schedule executive business reviews with 3 at-risk enterprise accounts
Draft proposal for enterprise onboarding specialist role and present to leadership
Update discount approval workflow in Salesforce

openQuestions: Should we offer multi-year commitment discounts (2-year: 10%, 3-year: 15%) or keep annual-only?
How do we handle existing customers on legacy pricing when new tiers launch?
Is there budget to hire 2 onboarding specialists in Q3 or should we wait for Q4?
unresolvedConflicts: Sales leadership wants aggressive discounting to win market share; Finance wants to maintain gross margin above 72%.
